svg.desc: Diverging stacked Likert chart: 7 statements on a 5-point scale from 'Strongly disagree' to 'Strongly agree'. The neutral option 'Neither agree nor disagree' is split in half across the centre line, so the zero rule marks the midpoint of the neutral segment rather than the boundary between agreement and disagreement. I understand how my work supports our strategy: 7% disagree, 11% neutral, 82% agree, net +76 points, n 900. My manager gives me useful feedback: 18% disagree, 16% neutral, 67% agree, net +49 points, n 900. I would recommend this company as a place to work: 18% disagree, 18% neutral, 64% agree, net +47 points, n 900. I have the tools I need to do my job well: 36% disagree, 13% neutral, 51% agree, net +16 points, n 900. I can grow my career here: 39% disagree, 23% neutral, 38% agree, net −1 points, n 900. My workload is sustainable: 56% disagree, 18% neutral, 27% agree, net −29 points, n 900. Decisions here are made quickly enough: 63% disagree, 14% neutral, 22% agree, net −41 points, n 900.

text.tspan: Source: Employee pulse survey, n = 900 per statement
Net = agree minus disagree, in pp; the neutral share counts on neither side.

'Neither agree nor disagree' is split evenly across the centre line, so the centre marks the middle of the neutral share, not the boundary between agreement and disagreement. Its share is printed once,
Not labelled on the chart: Disagree 4% (I understand how my work supports our strategy).
